correctness.rationale: For every n>=1 and m=2^n, semiconjugacy with circle doubling enumerates all distinct points of Fix(T^n). Interlaced rational coordinates occupy one quantile cell each. Rearrangement gives the unique cost formula for all p>=1. Exact arithmetic progression squared-offset sum proves W1 and W2 formulas, the atom at zero proves Winfty=1/m, and Riemann convergence of the two offset meshes plus a Lipschitz quadrature bound proves every fixed finite-p sharp constant. Convexity of quantile lengths supplies optimal at-most-m atomic benchmarks with arbitrary weights. A separate exact-rational inverse-branch checker verifies n=1..10 and higher integer moments. These finite checks are corroboration, not proof.

value.rationale: The empirical measure on all periodic points is a canonical, non-arbitrarily-selected approximation to the invariant Lebesgue law. This claim computes sharp all-order spatial transport quality and proves that deterministic periodic points, while attaining optimal order 2^{-n}, remain uniformly worse by a nontrivial p-dependent factor than the best possible quantizer; the effect persists through p=infinity. Such precise constants distinguish equidistribution from spatial design and can calibrate periodic-orbit quadrature and deterministic sampling. It is a natural dynamical invariant rather than a small finite table or a tautological reformulation.
